title: Warmth gave no clear link to skipped-stop shares in four US frog survey samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether first-stop temperature predicts skipped later stops on public frog survey routes. Four models used 8,771 NAAMP runs in the Northeast and Midwest in 2001-2008 and 2009-2015. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Slopes ranged from -0.24 to +0.19 percentage points per 5 C. The four-test intervals stayed within -0.93 to +0.70 percentage points. All retained runs had ten stop rows, so the outcome measured explicit skip flags. Route, observer, survey-window, year, season, wind and rain controls reduced some observation bias. A separate sparse calculation reproduced the main slopes. Selected nights, first-stop eligibility, few year clusters and unknown skip causes limit inference. These are conditional survey-effort links, not effects on species richness, climate trends or air pollution. Code, aggregate evidence and exact external source hashes are included.

display.caption: First-stop temperature slopes for skipped shares of stops 2-10. Four 98.75 percent intervals use the largest of route, year and two-way cluster errors. All cross zero.
